subtopics.name: Number pair analogy
question_types: number to number via arithmetic rule

subtopics.name: Linear seating
question_types: who sits where in a row

subtopics.name: Dice positions
question_types: opposite face from two/three dice positions

entries.name: Word-pair relationship
entries.statement: Name the exact relation in the given pair (synonym, antonym, worker-tool, country-river, item-category) and pick the option pair with the same relation.

entries.name: Number pair arithmetic rule
entries.statement: Find the linear rule linking the pair (a x k, a + k, a x k +/- c, digit operations) and test it on every option.

entries.name: Square/cube based number rule
entries.statement: Check whether one number is a square, cube, root or n^2 +/- c / n^3 +/- c of the other before trying linear rules.

entries.name: Number triad operation rule
entries.statement: Derive the operation that turns the outer numbers of a triad into the middle/last one (product, sum x k, (a x b) + c) and apply it to the set; never split numbers into digits unless told.

entries.name: Letter-cluster position shift
entries.statement: Write the alphabet position of each letter, compute the +/- shift per position (constant, alternating or increasing) and apply the same shifts to the target cluster.

entries.name: Letter-cluster gap pattern
entries.statement: Write the gaps between consecutive letters of each cluster (e.g. +2,+3) and pick the cluster whose gap pattern differs.

entries.name: Number pair odd-one-out rule
entries.statement: Find the rule linking the two numbers of each pair (multiple, square, n(n+1), ratio, prime gap) and pick the pair that breaks it.

entries.name: Number triad odd-one-out rule
entries.statement: Find the operation shared by the triads (product, sum x k, a + b = c) and pick the triad that fails it.

entries.name: Number property check
entries.statement: Test each number for a common property (prime, perfect square/cube, divisibility, digit sum) and pick the one without it.

entries.name: Word category membership
entries.statement: Put each word (or word pair) into its category or relation and pick the one that belongs to a different category.

entries.name: Repeating block fill-in
entries.statement: Guess the block length from the blank count and the letter count, write the series in blocks of that length and fill the blanks so every block is identical.

entries.name: Position-wise letter steps
entries.statement: Track each letter position of the clusters separately and find the +/- step of each position across terms.

entries.name: Split letter and number streams
entries.statement: Separate the letters and the numbers of each term into their own series and solve each one independently.

entries.name: First differences
entries.statement: Write the differences of consecutive terms and look for a constant, arithmetic or repeating pattern.

entries.name: Second-order differences
entries.statement: If the first differences are not constant, take differences again; a constant or odd-number second difference fixes the next term.

entries.name: Prime-number pattern
entries.statement: Check whether the terms or their differences are consecutive primes (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 ...).

entries.name: Squares and cubes pattern
entries.statement: Compare terms or differences with n^2, n^3 or n^2 +/- n before trying other rules.

entries.name: Multiply then add pattern
entries.statement: Check ratios of consecutive terms; if near-constant, test term x k +/- c (c constant or increasing n).

entries.name: Alternating two-series pattern
entries.statement: Split odd and even positioned terms (or alternate operations) and solve each sub-series separately.

entries.name: Letter position shift
entries.statement: Compare word and code letter by letter by alphabet position to find a constant, alternating or increasing shift, then apply it.

entries.name: Reverse then shift
entries.statement: If no direct shift fits, reverse the word first and then look for the per-letter shift.

entries.name: Vowel/consonant rule
entries.statement: Check whether vowels and consonants follow different rules (e.g. only consonants shift, vowels change to next vowel).

entries.name: Letter rearrangement
entries.statement: Code letters are the same as the word's but reordered (reversed, halves swapped, adjacent pairs swapped); map positions and apply.

entries.name: Common element elimination
entries.statement: Compare two coded sentences: the word common to both has the code common to both; eliminate to isolate the asked word.

entries.name: Letter position values
entries.statement: Replace each letter by its alphabet position (A=1 ... Z=26), possibly +/- a constant, and read the code.

entries.name: Sum/count of letter values
entries.statement: Code = sum of letter positions, possibly multiplied or offset by the number of letters; test sum, sum x n and sum +/- n.

entries.name: Reverse alphabet positions
entries.statement: Use reverse positions (Z=1 ... A=26, i.e. 27 minus position) for each letter, singly or summed.

entries.name: Decode symbol relations
entries.statement: Translate each symbol into a relation, draw it on a family tree with gender marks, and read the relation between the end persons.

entries.name: Family tree diagram
entries.statement: Draw generations as rows, mark + / - for gender and = for couples, then trace the path between the two persons.

entries.name: Pointing/introduction statements
entries.statement: Start from the end of the sentence ('my father's only son' = me) and work back to the speaker.

entries.name: Net displacement
entries.statement: Add up north-south and east-west moves separately; shortest distance = sqrt(NS^2 + EW^2) and direction from the signs.

entries.name: Turn tracking
entries.statement: Right turn = 90 deg clockwise, left = 90 deg anticlockwise; track facing direction after each turn on a compass grid.

entries.name: Rank from both ends
entries.statement: Total = rank from left + rank from right - 1; persons between A and B = |difference of positions| - 1.

entries.name: Comparison chain
entries.statement: Write all comparisons as one ordered chain (A > B > C) and read the extreme or middle element.

entries.name: Venn possible cases
entries.statement: Draw the minimal Venn diagram satisfying all statements, then accept a conclusion only if it holds in every possible case.

entries.name: Either-or complementary pair
entries.statement: When two conclusions about the same pair are individually uncertain but one must be true (Some/No), answer 'either I or II follows'.

entries.name: Venn region reading
entries.statement: Identify the region inside exactly the required shapes and outside the excluded ones, then read or add the numbers in those regions.

entries.name: Best-fit Venn diagram
entries.statement: Decide for each pair of classes whether one contains the other, they overlap, or are disjoint, then choose the diagram matching all pairs.

entries.name: Linear seating arrangement
entries.statement: Fix the person with the most definite clue first, draw blanks for seats, and place the rest clue by clue noting the facing direction.

entries.name: Circular seating arrangement
entries.statement: Fix one person, remember left/right flips for people facing the centre, and place others relative to fixed seats.

entries.name: Sign/symbol interchange
entries.statement: Rewrite the expression with the interchanged or substituted signs before evaluating anything.

entries.name: BODMAS evaluation
entries.statement: Evaluate brackets, then division and multiplication left to right, then addition and subtraction left to right.

entries.name: Swap trial to balance equation
entries.statement: Apply each option's swap (two numbers or two signs) and check which makes LHS = RHS; start with options that fix the size mismatch.

entries.name: Same operation across sets
entries.statement: Find one operation that turns the given numbers into the result in every complete set and apply it to the incomplete set.

entries.name: Row/column rule
entries.statement: Test the same operation along every row (then every column) of the grid to find the missing cell.

entries.name: Element tracking across frames
entries.statement: Follow one element at a time through the frames (path, step size, direction) and predict its next position.

entries.name: Fixed-angle rotation
entries.statement: Measure the rotation of each element per frame (45/90/135 deg, clockwise or anticlockwise) and continue it.

entries.name: Element addition/removal
entries.statement: Count elements (lines, dots, shapes) in each frame and continue the add/remove pattern.

entries.name: Position permutation of symbols
entries.statement: Number the positions in the frame and record where each symbol moves; repeat the same permutation for the next frame.

entries.name: Mirror image about a line
entries.statement: Flip every part across the mirror line: for a vertical mirror left and right swap, top and bottom stay; for a horizontal mirror the reverse.

entries.name: Water image
entries.statement: Water reflection flips top and bottom while left and right stay the same.

entries.name: Paper fold and unfold
entries.statement: Unfold one step at a time, mirroring every hole or cut across each fold line in reverse order of folding.

entries.name: Transparent sheet fold
entries.statement: Reflect the pattern on the folded half across the fold line and superimpose it on the other half.

entries.name: Embedded figure trace
entries.statement: Pick the most distinctive corner or line of the target shape and trace it in each option, keeping size and orientation fixed.

entries.name: Symmetry pattern completion
entries.statement: Use the figure's line(s) of symmetry to reconstruct the missing quarter from the opposite quarter.

entries.name: Common face rule
entries.statement: With a face common to two dice views, read the remaining faces in the same clockwise order from it; faces in the same position are opposite.

entries.name: Adjacent-face elimination
entries.statement: All faces seen together with a face are adjacent to it; the one face never seen with it is its opposite.

entries.name: Cyclic order of faces
entries.statement: Write the three visible faces in clockwise order for each view and align the views on a shared face to fix the rest.

entries.name: Cube net opposite faces
entries.statement: In an unfolded net, faces separated by exactly one face in a straight line are opposite; adjacent squares cannot be opposite.

entries.name: Painted cube counting
entries.statement: For an n x n x n cube painted on all faces: 3 faces = 8, 2 faces = 12(n-2), 1 face = 6(n-2)^2, none = (n-2)^3.

entries.name: Sort and compare positions
entries.statement: Write the word and its alphabetically sorted version one above the other and compare position by position.

entries.name: Letters between / gap count
entries.statement: Use alphabet positions (EJOTY anchors: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25) to count letters between two letters: gap = |p1 - p2| - 1.

entries.name: Opposite letter pairs
entries.statement: Opposite letter of a letter at position p is at 27 - p (A-Z, B-Y, C-X ...).

entries.name: Dictionary order
entries.statement: Compare words letter by letter from the left; the first differing letter decides the order.

entries.name: Systematic triangle count
entries.statement: Label all points and count triangles by size or by base line (a line cut into n segments with an apex gives n(n+1)/2), so none is missed.

entries.name: Square count by size
entries.statement: Count squares size by size; an n x n grid has sum of k^2 for k = 1..n squares.

entries.name: Line and shape enumeration
entries.statement: Label points and list each straight line or shape once by its end points, grouping by direction or size.
